title: In Search of Modernity: Conversion to Islam Among Ga People and the Politics of Religious Communities
content: The study analysis the conversion of Ga people into Islam who hitherto were adherents of African Traditional Religion and Christianity. The conversions bring to light the resilient of religion and challenges modernisation theory which envisages the decline of religion in public. Influenced by migrant Muslims to embrace Islam since 1900, the new converts founded ethnic based religious associations and built new settlements to practise pristine Islam by insulating themselves from the cultural influences of the latter including their indigenous Ga cultures. Though the converts succeeded in proselytising Islam among their kinsmen, they encountered challenges in intra-Ga Muslim politics and challenges of urbanisation.  Depended on archival and oral sources, the paper argues that the conversion of Ga people in the urban space of Accra illustrates the fact that the converts view Islam as representation of modernity which addresses their aspiration for meaning in life.
